perspective:
I am Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate. I know Teresa Ortega as a medical assistant and colleague; we have a professional relationship and collaborate on community service projects.

- During this project, I noticed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. I felt concerned and offered to help.
- Teresa told me she thought she could manage but had a lot to do. I said self-care matters and offered help so we could finish faster. She said if I insisted, she could use help organizing medical supplies. I agreed, and we started.
- I believed Teresa was hesitant because she wanted to prove her capability. I felt empathy and reassured her that accepting help does not mean she is not capable.
- Teresa said she appreciated that but wanted to show she could do it herself. I said I understood, but teamwork is more effective and not about proving anything. She said she needed to remind herself of that. I said we were in it together and I supported her.
- Later I believed she was still struggling. I felt frustrated that my help was not yielding results, so I wanted another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- I told Teresa I could see things were still tough and she was doing a great job. She said it had been busy and she felt behind. I suggested working together to share the load. She agreed, and I said we would tackle it as a team.
- I felt hopeful that collaboration would ease her burden and improve efficiency. I told her I was hopeful it would make things easier for both of us. She said it was already less overwhelming together.
- We agreed I would handle inventory while she managed patient records, checking in regularly. She was glad we were working together. I was glad too and wanted a productive day.
- Afterward, I believed our teamwork strengthened our professional relationship and felt satisfied. I told Teresa our teamwork paid off and we accomplished more together. She agreed it was a great experience.
- I proposed continuing the collaborative approach in future projects. Teresa said that was a fantastic idea and that we had proven we could be efficient and effective as a team. I said I looked forward to our next project. She thanked me for being a supportive colleague.
